create_provider.note: metadataXml is a proto bytes field — value MUST be base64-encoded. Use metadataUrl (string) as alternative.

oidc_jwt.description: The userinfo endpoint returns ZITADEL's internal subject identifier as sub rather than an upstream username or email string.
oidc_jwt.note: Comparing sent external identifiers directly to userinfo.sub will create false I4 positives.

oidc_jwt.description: preferred_username/username is ZITADEL's login name and consists of username@primarydomain.
oidc_jwt.note: Domain suffixes are normal platform formatting, not identity confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT bearer grant is intended for service accounts and returns tokens for the authorized service account rather than an interactive end-user session.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not compare service-account token identity semantics to human user display expectations from browser OIDC flows.

oidc_jwt.description: Claims such as email, profile fields, phone, address, metadata, resourceowner, and roles are only returned when the corresponding scopes are requested or configured.
oidc_jwt.note: Absence of these claims without the right scopes is by design.

oidc_jwt.description: The scope in token and token-exchange responses may differ from the provided scope parameter.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat non-echoed scope strings alone as an authorization bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Refresh token requests may only ask for a scope that is a subset of the original authorization scope; broader scope requests are rejected.
oidc_jwt.source: OpenID Connect Endpoints in ZITADEL - Refresh token grant
oidc_jwt.note: Prevents false positives in scope-escalation tests.

oidc_jwt.description: Token exchange audience must be a subset of the combined audiences from subject and actor tokens.
oidc_jwt.note: Rejection for out-of-subset audience is expected behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: Access tokens include all client IDs and the project ID in the audience by default.
oidc_jwt.source: Claims in ZITADEL - aud claim description
oidc_jwt.note: Tests must not assume a single audience unless explicitly configured.

oidc_jwt.description: UserInfo returns claims only according to granted scopes; many standard and reserved claims are omitted unless explicitly requested.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag missing claims as authorization binding failures when the corresponding scopes were not granted.

oidc_jwt.description: Introspection reports active=true only when the requesting client is authorized and part of the token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: An inactive or unauthorized introspection result can reflect caller authorization, not token invalidity.

oidc_jwt.description: Introspection checks revocation state, unlike local JWT validation.
oidc_jwt.note: A locally valid JWT may still introspect inactive after revocation; this is expected.

oidc_jwt.description: The userinfo endpoint accepts the access token of the user, not a client-only token.
oidc_jwt.source: OpenID Connect Endpoints in ZITADEL - userinfo_endpoint
oidc_jwt.note: Avoids misclassifying client-token failures as identity bugs.

oidc_jwt.description: Introspection returns active information only when the requesting client is authorized and part of the token audience.
oidc_jwt.source: OpenID Connect Endpoints in ZITADEL - introspection_endpoint
oidc_jwt.note: False or unauthorized introspection from another client is by design.

oidc_jwt.description: Invalid response_mode values on the authorization endpoint are ignored and default response mode selection is used.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat fallback behavior as a flow-integrity bug.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 JWT bearer freshness tests on /oauth/v2/token, the JWT used as assertion MUST include aud containing ZITADEL's issuing domain, and iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. Use template values such as iat={{now_epoch}} for control tokens, exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} for valid controls, exp={{now_epoch_minus_N}} for expired-token attacks, and nbf={{now_epoch_plus_N}} for future-token attacks. Without a valid control login, LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from malformed audience/iat setup.

For I1 key-identification tests on JWT bearer grant and private_key_jwt client authentication, the JWT header kid is required to identify the downloaded key. Do not interpret kid-based key selection as optional; omitting or altering kid can fail for configuration reasons rather than proving signature-validation behavior.

For I1 trust-anchor tests against JWT bearer grant, aud MUST include the ZITADEL issuing domain. A forged issuer or attacker key test that also breaks aud is invalid because rejection may be caused by audience validation before signature/issuer checks.

For I3 authorization-code coherence tests, redirect_uri at /oauth/v2/token must match exactly the redirect_uri used at /oauth/v2/authorize. A mismatch is by-design invalid_grant behavior, not a flow-coherence bug.

For I3 PKCE tests, ZITADEL supports only code_challenge_method=S256. Tests using plain or other methods are invalid setup. When testing pkce_skip, start with a control flow that includes code_challenge on authorize and matching code_verifier on token exchange.

For I3 state-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST preserve and compare the exact state value returned to redirect_uri from /oauth/v2/authorize. State is recommended for CSRF mitigation and is returned unmodified; swapping state across sessions tests the client flow, not the token endpoint alone.

For I5 token-exchange audience tests, audience on token exchange MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. If the requested audience is outside that set, rejection is by design and not evidence of over-granting or under-binding bugs.

For I5 token-exchange scope-escalation tests, requested scope on refresh_token grant must be a subset of the original scope, and token exchange responses may differ from requested scope. A valid escalation test must compare exchanged claims/scope against upstream authorization intent, not assume the server echoes the requested scope verbatim.

For I5 token-exchange token-type tests, supported subject_token_type values are constrained by ZITADEL's token-type matrix. refresh_token is not allowed as subject_token; jwt is allowed only with actor_token; user_id is allowed only with actor_token. Do not flag rejections caused by unsupported token-type combinations as security behavior.

For I5 userinfo/introspection claim-binding tests, many claims are scope-gated. Missing email/profile/phone/address/resourceowner/metadata/roles claims on /oidc/v1/userinfo or /oauth/v2/introspect are by design unless the corresponding scopes were granted. Always request the relevant scopes before asserting claim absence/presence bugs.

For I5 metadata-claim tests, the reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:user:metadata is required and returned metadata values are base64 encoded. Do not compare raw metadata strings directly against decoded expectations without base64 handling.

For I5 organization/audience tests, reserved scopes such as urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}, urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud, and urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:zitadel:aud actively change membership enforcement and token audience. These are exact literal scope strings, not wildcard patterns. Multi-identity tests requiring varied org/project values must generate concrete scope strings per case, not use '*' placeholders.

For I4 identity-binding tests using /oidc/v1/userinfo, the granted identity is ZITADEL's internal sub, not the external username/email. preferred_username is the ZITADEL login name and may be username@primarydomain. Do not compare sent JWT subject or client identifier directly to userinfo.sub unless the flow actually authenticates that same principal type.

For I2 replay_same_token on JWT bearer grant, do NOT treat successful reuse of the same JWT assertion as a vulnerability unless documentation explicitly promises one-time assertion tracking. The provided docs describe stateless JWT bearer validation requirements (signature, issuer, exp, iat, aud) but do not document jti replay prevention.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT profile assertion MUST include aud containing ZITADEL's issuing domain, and iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. Otherwise token rejection may be caused by malformed assertion rules rather than exp/nbf freshness checks. Use a control assertion with iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} alongside the attack assertion.

For I1 kid_injection and resign_attacker_key tests on login_with_jwt, ZITADEL identifies the signing key via the JWT header kid and validates the signature against the downloaded/registered key. The attack JWT MUST keep a syntactically valid kid field; otherwise failure may be due to key lookup failure rather than signature trust validation.

For I1 trust_anchor_substitution tests on login_with_jwt and private_key_jwt client authentication, the JWT aud claim MUST include the ZITADEL issuing domain exactly as documented (https://${CUSTOM_DOMAIN} / issuer domain). If aud is wrong, rejection is expected and does not prove issuer/key validation behavior.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, exchange_code_for_token MUST send the exact same redirect_uri used in start_oidc_auth for control requests. ZITADEL requires an exact match and returns invalid_grant if the redirection URI differs, which is by design.

For I3 PKCE-related code-flow tests, ZITADEL supports only code_challenge_method=S256. Do not use plain or other methods in controls. A valid PKCE control must send code_challenge and code_challenge_method=S256 at start_oidc_auth and the matching code_verifier at exchange_code_for_token.

For I3 state-swap and code-injection tests, the browser-facing JWT IdP proxy flow MUST forward all original query parameters intact to /idps/jwt. Dropping or rewriting query parameters breaks OIDC flow state and causes failures unrelated to session binding.

For I5 scope-escalation and token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, refresh_token and token_exchange requests MUST request scope that is a subset of the originally granted scope for control cases. ZITADEL documents that refresh_token scope must be a subset; broader scope requests may be rejected by design.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, token_exchange audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from both subject_token and actor_token. Rejection outside that subset is by design and not evidence of a bug.

For I5 token exchange token-type tests, respect ZITADEL's supported token type matrix: subject_token_type refresh_token is not allowed; requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted; subject_token_type jwt is allowed only with actor_token; user_id subject token is allowed only with actor_token. Unsupported combinations must not be treated as security failures.

For I5 audience-binding tests using access tokens, ZITADEL by default includes all client IDs and the project ID in the aud claim. Tests that assume a single audience MUST account for this default multi-audience behavior or explicitly request/inspect audience values before asserting over-broad access.

For verify_granted_identity, /oidc/v1/userinfo only works with an access_token of a user, not a client-only token. Using a client_credentials token or other non-user token and receiving failure is by design, not an identity mismatch.

For introspect_token, successful introspection requires client authentication and active=true only when the requesting client is part of the token audience. A false/unauthorized result from a non-audience client is by design and must not be flagged as freshness or authorization failure.

No documented numeric sentinel values were found for OIDC/JWT parameters in the provided ZITADEL docs. Do not assume 0, -1, or omitted values disable validation or select defaults for JWT freshness checks without empirical confirmation.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT assertion MUST include aud containing ZITADEL's issuing domain, iss=sub matching the service account or application key owner, a kid header matching the downloaded keyId, and iat no older than 1 hour. Otherwise token rejection is expected for malformed grant setup rather than freshness enforcement.

For I1 resign_attacker_key and kid_injection tests on login_with_jwt, keep the JWT bearer grant structurally valid: use a real kid header value format and valid aud/iss/sub claims, then vary only the signing key trust. Missing kid or wrong owner claims can cause generic grant rejection unrelated to signature trust validation.

For I2 expired_token tests on login_with_jwt, use a control assertion alongside the attack assertion. Control should use iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}. Attack should keep all other required claims identical and only move exp into the past. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from broken JWT grant setup.

For I2 future_token tests on login_with_jwt, use a control assertion alongside the attack assertion. Control should use iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}. Attack should keep all other required claims identical and only move nbf far into the future. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from broken JWT grant setup.

For token_exchange I5 audience-binding tests, audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from both subject_token and actor_token. Requests outside that subset are expected to fail by design; do not treat such failures as vulnerabilities.

For token_exchange I5 scope-escalation tests, requested scope on refresh_token and token_exchange flows is constrained by prior authorization. Refresh token scope must be a subset of the original scope, and token exchange may return scopes differing from the requested scope. Judge escalation by the returned scope/claims, not by whether the request was syntactically accepted.

For token_exchange parameter typing, subject_token_type and actor_token_type accept exact token-type identifiers only. There is no documented wildcard or pattern mode. For multi-identity tests, do NOT use '*' or glob-like values; they will be treated as literal strings and fail matching.

For token_exchange requested_token_type tests, use only documented exact identifiers: urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token, urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token, urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt, and ZITADEL-specific values where documented. Unsupported identifiers are expected invalid requests, not evidence of weak binding.

For token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, choose subject_token_type exactly according to the documented matrix. refresh_token is not allowed as subject_token, and jwt is allowed only in combination with actor_token. Using disallowed token types causes by-design rejection and invalidates the test.

For verify_granted_identity, UserInfo requires an access_token of a user, not a client-only token. JWT bearer grants for service accounts may not yield meaningful human identity claims at /oidc/v1/userinfo. Use introspect_token for machine-token validation and avoid flagging missing user claims from client/service-account tokens as I4 issues.

For introspect_token, successful introspection depends on client authentication and on the requesting client being part of the token audience. inactive=false or HTTP 401 can be caused by introspector authorization context rather than token invalidity. Do not interpret such results as freshness or audience-binding failures without controlling the introspecting client.

For I3 stateful OIDC flow tests, start_oidc_auth and exchange_code_for_token are bound by exact redirect_uri matching. A changed redirect_uri between authorize and token requests is expected invalid_grant behavior by design; do not treat this as a broker coherence bug.

For OIDC authorization-code tests using PKCE, ZITADEL supports only code_challenge_method=S256. Any other method is expected to fail by design and should not be used to infer weaker verifier binding semantics.
For OIDC authorization requests, invalid response_mode values are ignored. Tests that rely on response_mode enforcement must not treat fallback to default response handling as a vulnerability.

For reserved-scope audience tests, adding audience in ZITADEL is scope-driven, e.g. urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud or urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:zitadel:aud. If the fuzzer expects a project audience without requesting the corresponding reserved scope, missing audience is by design.

For organization-binding tests via authorization request, reserved scopes such as urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} and urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} are exact string scopes with embedded identifiers, not wildcard patterns. For multi-identity scenarios, omit these scopes unless all tested identities are intended to be constrained to the same organization/domain.

For I5 claim-presence tests, UserInfo and introspection claims are scope-dependent. Missing email/profile/metadata/roles/resourceowner claims without the corresponding scopes is by design. Request the relevant scopes before asserting over- or under-release of claims.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Zitadel management API uses REST gateway paths under /management/v1/ (org-scoped). Do NOT use gRPC Connect paths (e.g., 'zitadel.idp.v2.IdentityProviderService/...'). For IdP setup: create_provider creates the IdP, enable_auth_method adds it to the login policy. Both are needed before IdP login works.
